key_insight: CVD-grown single-crystalline cubic D0₃-Fe₃Ge nanoplates exhibit robust anomalous Hall behavior, with calculations linking epitaxial strain to enhanced Berry-curvature-driven conductivity.
engineering_relevance: These epitaxial ferromagnetic nanoplates offer a potential platform for spintronic devices operating above room temperature.
method: CVD synthesis and structural characterization of cubic D0₃-Fe₃Ge nanoplates.
SQUID magnetometry, magnetotransport, and second-harmonic generation measurements.
DFT calculations of strain-induced band reconstruction and anomalous Hall conductivity.
evidence_signal: Structural analysis indicates ~4.16% interfacial compressive strain; transport scaling supports an intrinsic AHE mechanism, while DFT predicts roughly doubled anomalous Hall conductivity consistent with experiment.
watch_item: Strain relaxes toward the surface, making thickness-dependent strain control an important concern for reproducible device integration.
paper_title: Robust Anomalous Hall Effect in Epitaxial Cubic D0$_3$-Fe$_3$Ge Nanoplates Grown by Chemical Vapor Deposition
